findings.evidence: The original final condition called sfSourceFor before yielding the final BunFile.arrayBuffer read. The actual registration scope could revoke the capability while that read was pending; evaluation would resume after the authority check and could return a receipt.
findings.change: Await the final actual file bytes before the synchronous source-capability, physical-path, content and digest guard. No asynchronous operation follows the final capability check before receipt return.
findings.regression: skill-source-boundary.test.ts holds completion of the second real arrayBuffer read after real bytes are obtained, closes the actual public host scope, observes sfSourceFor become undefined and requires skill-source-changed instead of a receipt.

limits: No local test or typecheck was executed; all prepared tests require the parent-owned surgical hosted run.
A persisted synthetic Session message is the engine's real skill-context message. It is not a model output or a fabricated native receipt.
No provider turn, Task admission, Relay admission or Schedule admission is attempted. Mission64 owns those paths.
SkillLoadReceipt runId labels in these component tests are synthetic. Real receipt evidence consists of the observed Session ID/message ID and verified source/instruction/profile/manifest digests.

The tests qualify skill loading and profile registration. They do not by themselves satisfy AM01's persisted business output and product consumer requirements, AM03's complete user/project authorization requirements or G7's full native execution obligations.

No Session get validation was added to the loader: the actual native host already checks the created Session identity, agent, location and model before loading and product authority revalidates the Session before binding. No independent caller bug was demonstrated.
The test host uses the public production composition and actual Location routing; it does not use the core test harness whose withRunner ignores the requested Session ID.
